newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks resisted a slump on Wall Street and continued their mild-mannered advance Monday, closing higher in selective trading, dealers said.

"It was a very quiet session, but stocks outperformed bonds and the outlook remains good," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities. "I think activity will start to pick up towards the middle of the week, when the private pension funds start pumping more money into the markets."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.6 percent to 707.16, stretching gains so far in February to 2.0 percent.

"The MerVal is still aiming stubbornly for 728 (where it capped a long upward march in January 1994) but it may take longer to get there than we thought because market conditions are still overbought," another trader said. "We could also see profit-taking ahead of next week's options expirations."

Traders said bidding would remain selective and favor some second-line stocks which turned in good quarterly results. Among them are power generator Capex and Citicorp Equity Investments, which posted the day's strongest gains of 9.8 percent and 8.8 percent, respectively. CEI was initiated as a buy Monday by ING Barings.
The broad market index closed up 0.5 percent, with winners outpacing losers 24 to 18 and 18 issues closing flat.
Broad market volume shrank to 21.4 million pesos from 26.2 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to 79.5 million pesos from 126.8 million Friday.

Sharpest MerVal risers were energy firm Central Costanera, steelmaker Siderca and foods giant Molinos, up 3.5 percent, 3.4 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively. Losers were led by pulp maker Celulosa, which tumbled 7.0 percent, and carmaker Ciadea and petrochemical firm Indupa, both off 1.3 percent.
